text:
Impact Mozambique 2026 Concludes With Mass Baptisms and Renewed Mission Commitment
Thousands of Seventh-day Adventists gathered at Zimpeto National Stadium in Maputo, Mozambique, on May 23 to close Impact Mozambique 2026 with worship, baptisms, and renewed commitments to mission. This, according to an article from Adventist Review, by Marcos Paseggi.
The celebration featured cheerful singing, biblical preaching, and a nationwide baptismal initiative that church leaders said extended to more than 660 sites across the country. Baptisms were conducted in oceans, rivers, lakes, pools, and other locations as pastors and regional leaders led ceremonies throughout Mozambique.
Southern Africa-Indian Ocean Division president Harrington Akombwa thanked the Mozambican government for supporting the initiative:
“We would like to thank the government of Mozambique,” Akombwa said.
“Thank you for creating the conditions and embracing us.”
Government representative Eduardo Joaquim Mulémbwè, speaking on behalf of President Daniel Chapo, praised the Adventist Church for promoting peace, moral values, education, health care, and social cohesion:
“The government of the Republic of Mozambique fully acknowledges the role of religious organizations in promoting peace, fostering social cohesion, and advocating for ethical and moral values,” Mulémbwè said.
He also highlighted what he described as the church’s “culture of hope, active responsibility, and commitment to one’s neighbor.”
General Conference president Erton Köhler urged members to actively participate in God’s mission and emphasized unity within the worldwide Adventist Church:
“I like seeing this church as a family, under one Father, purchased by the same blood, and belonging to the same nation—the heavenly kingdom,” Köhler said.
“We have the same message, the same mission, and the same hope of seeing Jesus’ soon return.”
Köhler also challenged members to take an active role in evangelism:
“The gospel will be preached with or without us, but I believe miracles will be more striking if we join the effort.”
Church leaders also highlighted OneVoice27, a global evangelism initiative leading up to 2027 that encourages members to use personal ministry and digital platforms to share the message of Jesus.
Calling attendees to raise their cell phones, Köhler encouraged members to dedicate their social media presence to mission outreach:
“OneVoice27 has already started.
“We are ready to launch a mass movement from the palm of our hands.”
